note: One people, tradition or figure from history for every country in Asia. Siachen Glacier is left out: nobody lives there but soldiers.

AFG.name: Buzkashi rider
AFG.note: A game of horsemen, played across a whole field with no ball.

ARE.name: Falconer
ARE.note: A hunting bird that sits on your glove and comes back to it.

ARM.name: Khachkar carver
ARM.note: Cross-stones cut in lace, no two of them the same.

AZE.name: Ashik
AZE.note: A travelling singer who carries the news and the old stories.

BGD.name: Baul singer
BGD.note: Wandering minstrels who own almost nothing but their songs.

BHR.name: Pearl diver
BHR.note: Down on one breath with a stone, up with a basket of oysters.

BRN.name: Kampong Ayer boatman
BRN.note: A whole town on stilts above the river, older than the cars.

BTN.name: Cham dancer
BTN.note: Masked dances that whirl in the courtyard of a mountain fortress.

CYN.name: Karagöz puppeteer
CYN.note: Shadow puppets of camel leather, played behind a lit sheet.

CYP.name: Lefkara lace maker
CYP.note: A needle, white thread, and a pattern learned from a grandmother.

GEO.name: Khevsur
GEO.note: Mountain villagers who still wore chainmail a century ago.

HKG.name: Lion dancer
HKG.note: Two people inside one lion, dancing it up a pole for luck.

IDN.name: Balinese dancer
IDN.note: Every finger and every eye moves, and none of it by accident.

IOA.name: Cocos Malay
IOA.note: Islanders of a ring of coral, halfway to nowhere.

IRN.name: Persian carpet weaver
IRN.note: A garden, drawn in knots, that takes a year to finish.

IRQ.name: Marsh Arab
IRQ.note: Houses of reed on islands of reed, in the marshes of two rivers.

ISR.name: Klezmer musician
ISR.note: A clarinet that laughs and cries in the same tune.

JOR.name: Bedouin
JOR.note: Black goat-hair tents pitched among the red rocks of Wadi Rum.

KAZ.name: Eagle hunter
KAZ.note: A golden eagle on the arm, trained to hunt across the steppe.

KGZ.name: Manaschi
KGZ.note: Tellers of the Manas: a poem longer than any book, held in the head.

KHM.name: Apsara dancer
KHM.note: The dancers carved on the walls of Angkor, still dancing.

KOR.name: Haenyeo
KOR.note: The sea women of Jeju, who dive without air tanks, well into old age.

KWT.name: Dhow builder
KWT.note: Ships sewn and pegged together, built by eye without a plan.

LAO.name: Hmong
LAO.note: Mountain people whose stitched cloth tells whole stories.

LBN.name: Phoenician sailor
LBN.note: Traders who sailed the whole Mediterranean and gave us the alphabet.

LKA.name: Kandyan dancer
LKA.note: Silver headdresses, and drums that answer every step.

MAC.name: Macanese
MAC.note: Four hundred years of Portugal and China in one kitchen.

MMR.name: Inle leg-rower
MMR.note: Fishermen who row standing up, with one leg wrapped round the oar.

MYS.name: Iban
MYS.note: Whole villages under one long roof, on the rivers of Borneo.

NPL.name: Sherpa
NPL.note: People of the high valleys, at home where the air is thin.

OMN.name: Frankincense harvester
OMN.note: Cut the bark, wait, and collect the tears the tree makes.

PAK.name: Kalash
PAK.note: Three valleys, their own gods, and festivals full of flowers.

PHL.name: Ifugao
PHL.note: Rice terraces cut into the mountain two thousand years ago.

PRK.name: Korean drum dancer
PRK.note: A small drum at the waist, played while spinning.

PSX.name: Tatreez embroiderer
PSX.note: Cross-stitch in red thread, where every village has its own pattern.

QAT.name: Falconer
QAT.note: A hunting bird that sits on your glove and comes back to it.

SGP.name: Peranakan
SGP.note: Chinese and Malay together for centuries — in the tiles, the beads and the food.

SYR.name: Palmyrene trader
SYR.note: Caravan merchants of a city of columns in the middle of the desert.

THA.name: Khon dancer
THA.note: Masked theatre of monkeys and giants, from an ancient story.

TJK.name: Pamiri
TJK.note: People of the roof of the world, on the highest road there is.

TKM.name: Akhal-Teke rider
TKM.note: Desert horses with coats that shine like metal.

TLS.name: Tais weaver
TLS.note: Cloth woven for welcomes, weddings and goodbyes.

TUR.name: Whirling dervish
TUR.note: One hand up, one hand down, turning for an hour without stopping.

TWN.name: Amis
TWN.note: The largest of the island's first peoples, and their harvest songs.

UZB.name: Silk Road merchant
UZB.note: Samarkand: where the caravans from China met the ones from Rome.

VNM.name: Water puppeteer
VNM.note: Puppets danced on a flooded rice field, the poles hidden below.

YEM.name: Socotri
YEM.note: Islanders who live among trees that grow nowhere else on Earth.
